name: Oblique Facial Cleft

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Oblique Facial Cleft

criteria.description: Presence of an oblique facial cleft extending from the lip or oral commissure towards the eye or nose
Involvement of the lower eyelid or infraorbital region with soft tissue and/or bony defects
Presence of associated craniofacial anomalies such as cleft lip, cleft palate, or nasal deformities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic oblique facial cleft with orbital involvement, with or without associated craniofacial anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging to assess bony involvement

imaging: CT scan demonstrating bony defects along the oblique facial cleft
MRI to evaluate soft tissue and orbital involvement
genetic: No specific gene identified; may be sporadic or part of syndromic presentations
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic facial cleft morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Tessier clefts include a broader classification of craniofacial clefts with different anatomical locations
Oblique facial cleft specifically involves the oblique line from oral commissure to infraorbital region
Isolated cleft lip and/or palate lacks the oblique extension towards the orbit
Absence of lower eyelid coloboma or infraorbital bony defects

redFlags: Severe orbital involvement causing vision impairment
Respiratory distress due to airway obstruction
references: Tessier P. Anatomical classification of facial clefts. J Maxillofac Surg. 1976
Craniofacial Anomalies: Diagnosis and Management, 2nd Edition
